requiredFindings.title: Verify that exhaustion precedes work, not only that it preserves the ledger prefix
requiredFindings.description: The independent model and per-site accounting loops compare totals and WorkLedger::used, but do not record allocations, comparisons or pushes actually performed. A comparison moved before compare(work)? has the same successful total and the same used prefix when the subsequent charge refuses; the extra unfunded comparison is invisible to these tests. The submitted 20 mutations remove charges or change prices, but omit the accepted plan's explicit mutation of a probe charged after its comparison. No production-source charge-order guard is present either. Thus the submitted controls establish charge amounts/prefixes but not the plan's required before-work property, despite SCOPE's claim that the per-site tests establish it.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Add an operation-order oracle for the production allocation/comparison/fill sites, or a complete reviewed source-order guard in the style of the existing kernel controls, alongside the independent accounting model. Require exhaustion before the corresponding work, including both predicate passes and policy probes/order checks. Add the planned probe-charge-after-comparison mutation and an allocation-before-charge mutation; both must fail assertions without relying on compile failure. Retain the current exact-total and prefix tests, and describe precisely what each control proves.
requiredFindings.validationExpectation: A mutant that stores slice[mid].borrow().cmp(key) before compare(work)? and matches on the stored result afterward must be caught. Likewise catch allocating a result/index buffer before its refused charge. On the unmutated candidate, per-site short allowances must show no operation at or past the refused site, not merely no further ledger debit. Supply the corresponding successful controls and mutation evidence through the authorized implementation lane.
